The appellant in Crl.A.No.744/2023 is accused No.1 and appellants in Crl.A.No.701/2023 are accused Nos.2 and 3 respectively.

Both the appeals arise out of crime No.135/2022 of Nanjanagudu Town Police Station, Mysore registered for the offences punishable under Sections 403, 406, 420 and 114 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter referred to as the "IPC" for short) and under Section 9 of The Karnataka Protection of Interest of Depositors in Financial Establishments Act, 2004 (KPIDFE Act, for short).

The Court of Prl.District and Sessions Judge at Mysuru vide order dated 03.03.2023 passed in Crl.Misc.No.133/2023 and Crl.Misc.No.122/2023 has rejected the applications filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. by accused Nos.1 to 3, which has resulted in filing these appeals under Section 16 of the KPIDFE Act.

sentences.text:
3. Heard the learned counsel for the appellants and learned High Court Government Pleader for the State and perused the material available on record.
NC: 2024:KHC:10234 4.

In the complaint lodged by Manjunatha B, he has alleged that one Shambulingu M., working as a teacher, induced him to open an account in a chit fund run by him in the name of his wife Smt.B Dakshayini (accused No.1) and upon his insistence, he joined a chit for Rs.2,50,000/- on 15.06.2019 and paid Rs.5,000/- through Phone Pay every month.
The said chit ended on 15.09.2022 and again he joined a chit and paid Rs.5,000/- for about eight months, but later, he came to know that the said Shambulingu committed suicide.

When he went and requested accused No.1 to return the chit amount, the said accused without repaying the amount vacated the house and fled away etc.
5.

It is alleged that accused No.1 and her husband collected huge amount from many depositors and cheated them and from the proceeds, they purchased properties in the name of accused Nos.2 and 3,
none other than the father and brother of accused No.1.

The learned HCGP contended that accused Nos.1 to 3 have colluded with each other and persuaded the public to join the chit and received deposits from various persons and after collecting huge amount, cheated them.
He contends that in the present case the complainant has been cheated to the tune of Rs.2,90,000/-.

He further contended that the petition preferred under Section 438 of Cr.P.C is not maintainable, since the accused have committed an offence under the KPIDFE Act and in view of Section 18 (2) of the said act, the learned Sessions Judge has rightly rejected the prayer seeking anticipatory bail.

7. The learned Sessions Judge relying on a decision of this Court in Shreesha Sasithota Pabhakaran Vs. The State of Karnataka (Crl.P.No.9971/2022) dated 10.11.2022 rejected the prayer seeking anticipatory bail, observing that the provisions of Section 438 of Cr.P.C. are not applicable, since the KPIDFE Act has overriding effect, over all other provisions of Law.

entities.text: Shreesha Sasithota Pabhakaran Vs. The State of Karnataka (Crl.P.No.9971/2022)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is NC: 2024:KHC:10234 observed that, in this case Section 9 of the KPIDFE Act, 2004 is invoked and therefore, the accused are not entitled for the grant of anticipatory bail, as the very petition is not maintainable in view of the clear bar under Section 18 (2) of the said Act.

8. One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the appellants is that Section 9 of the KPIDFE Act is not applicable to the case on hand, since the definition of "deposit" does not include the amount received by way of subscription, in respect of a chit.

It is therefore contended by the learned counsel that the decision referred to by the learned Sessions Judge is not applicable and the Shri. M. Basavanna vs State Of Karnataka on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176156627/
4 learned Sessions Judge was not right in rejecting the petition seeking anticipatory bail holding that the same is not maintainable in view of Section 18(2) of the KPIDFE Act.
9.

Shri. M. Basavanna vs State Of Karnataka on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176156627/
4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the definition of "deposit" provided under Section 2(2) (vii) of KPIDFE Act, "deposit" does not include the amount received by way of subscription in respect of a NC: 2024:KHC:10234 chit.

In the present case, the offence alleged under the KPIDFE Act is one under Section 9 of the said Act,
i.e., any financial establishment fraudulently committing default in the repayment of 'deposit' etc.

Hence, it cannot be said that a prima facie case is made out against the appellants, at this stage,
which would attract the provisions of the said act.

10. The allegations against the appellants are that they have cheated the complainant after receiving the chit subscription in a sum of Rs.2,90,000/- and then failed to return the said amount and further that the proceeds collected from similar other depositors were invested by acquiring various assets etc., in the name of accused Nos.2 and 3 and thereby cheated the complainant.
11.

A perusal of the complaint averments would reveal that one Shambulingu, working as a teacher,
met the complainant and he insisted him to join the chit which was being run in the name of his wife i.e., accused No.1.
The said Shambulingu committed suicide on 03.11.2022.

NC: 2024:KHC:10234 The allegations are that on coming to know about him committing suicide,
when the complainant requested accused No.1 to return the amount, initially she promised that the amount would be returned, but later the said accused vacated the house and fled away and all the accused in collusion with each other, cheated the complainant and similar other depositors.
12. The prosecution has to establish it's case in due course.
The offences alleged are not punishable with death or imprisonment for life.
During the pendency of these appeals, interim bail was granted to the appellants.
It is submitted that the appellants have appeared before the Investigating Officer and executed the bond as specified in the order, with a surety and co-operated with the investigation.
13. In the above facts and circumstances, the relief sought in these appeals can be granted by imposing necessary conditions.

Accordingly the following:
- 10 -  NC: 2024:KHC:10234  ORDER  i) Appeals are allowed.
